messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert flood detected: 142 PD incidents in the last 5m for service=inference-serve-err. Auto-created incident channel.
olivia: I'm on it, seeing tons of pages come through. Initial triage: spikes in 504s to model servers after a small canary rollout.
olivia: @ben @kai tagging you for help — can anyone confirm if a recent deploy went out to production?
deploy-bot: deploy-2026-03-15-18:23 rolled to inference-pool-3 by anna.
ben: yep saw that deploy, but metric surge looks more like connection timeouts than model output errors. Logs show upstream timeouts to redis-cache on some nodes.
kai: interesting — I just checked KV cache hit rates: dropped from ~98% to 54% coincident with the rollout. Could be a cache key change in the new model binary.
olivia: customer-facing impact: a subset of requests are 504ing, roughly 2% of requests for critical customers (pg id: cust-423, cust-901). PD priority: P1 pages are noisy but limited impact.
olivia: I'll start a short mitigation: suppress repeated PD pages while we investigate. Planning to do a temporary grouping + rate limit. Any objections?
ben: +1. We should avoid blanket squelch. Do per-alert dedupe based on fingerprint: service+model-version+error-code. That will keep different root causes paged.
anna: can you drop the exact Prometheus alert rule you want me to change? I can patch Alertmanager.
ben: tentative promql we used earlier: 
```
sum by (service, model, code) (increase(http_request_errors_total{service="inference"}[5m])) > 10
```
Change to use `model_version` label and add `unless` for known transient codes? Better approach is Alertmanager grouping config: group_by: ["service","model_version","error_code"] and add `repeat_interval: 10m` for these alerts for now.
olivia: I'll apply a temporary rate-limit on PagerDuty for this alert group to 1 page per 10m while we debug. Can someone on SRE own the rollback if it causes missed pages?
kai: I'll own rollback. Also creating a tiny dashboard panel to show pages per 1m by model_version so we can watch. Query I'll add to Grafana: 
```
sum by(model_version) (increase(pagerduty_pages_total{alertname=~"inference.*"}[1m]))
```
anna: patching Alertmanager now: adding `group_by: ["service","model_version","error_code"]` and `repeat_interval: 10m`. Pushing config via `kubectl -n monitoring apply -f alertmanager-patch.yaml`
anna: applied. Alertmanager reloaded successfully.
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty rule updated: dedupe grouping enabled for key {service,model_version,error_code}; rate-limit applied: 1 notification / 10m for grouped events.
olivia: thanks. Confirming pages are down to reasonable levels — still seeing unique alerts but not the storm.
ben: digging into logs: root cause looks like the new model does a slightly different tokenization and created a hot-spot on a small subset of cache keys. Some nodes evict frequently causing downstream timeouts to redis.
kai: rolling back the model on a single canary node to confirm: `kubectl -n inference set image deploy/model-worker model=image:previous`
kai: after rollback on canary, cache hit rate goes back to ~97% on that node and 504s drop for traffic pinned to it.
olivia: that's a clear repro. Next steps?
ben: short term: rollback the full rollout until we patch the model keying logic. Medium term: add a pre-deploy synthetic that exercises heavy cache key patterns.
kai: agreed. I'll open a Jira: INFRA-3145 to track code fix + canary test. Assign to @kai and @anna.
olivia: I'm going to hand off oncall to @ben for the next 2 hours while I coordinate comms with customer success. Ben, you'll own the monitoring checks and rollback progress.
ben: taking handoff. I'll keep the thread updated every 15m.
olivia: CS update — reached out to cust-423 and cust-901, they saw elevated errors but accepted the rollback ETA. No major production-data loss.
ben: ops notes for post-incident: 1) add alert fingerprinting to Alertmanager as permanent, 2) add a new Grafana panel for "pages by model_version/error_code" in the incident runbook dashboard, 3) create a playbook snippet for temporary PD rate limits and who is authorized to apply them.
ben: sample Alertmanager mute command we used (for runbook): 
```
# mute noisy grouping for 10m via API
curl -XPOST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' https://alertmanager.example/api/v2/silences -d '{"matchers":[{"name":"alertname","value":"inference-errors"},{"name":"model_version","value":"v2.1.4"}],"startsAt":"2026-03-15T18:40:00Z","endsAt":"2026-03-15T18:50:00Z","createdBy":"oncall","comment":"temporary suppression during investigation"}'
```
anna: created INFRA-3145 and INFRA-3146 (dashboard + runbook updates). Links: https://jira.redwood/INFRA-3145 https://jira.redwood/INFRA-3146
kai: I'm also pushing a small canary test harness to the CI job that will simulate cache key distribution. Will follow up in the PR.
ben: agreed follow-up owners: ben (oncall/monitoring), kai (fix + canary tests), anna (alertmanager/dashboard changes).
olivia: thanks team. I'll write a short incident summary for leadership and include customer impact, actions taken, and follow-ups. Tagging this for a 1-hour postmortem tomorrow 10:00 PT.
olivia: closing the immediate paging storm — reassigning to post-incident channel after this. If anyone sees regression, reopen this thread. :white_check_mark:
